video_title: Shams Charania confirms Jaylen Brown did NOT put in a formal trade request 👀 | SportsCenter

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics trade Jaylen Brown to 76ers for Paul George and picks
quotes.excerpt: When you dangle Jaylen Brown in trade talks with Giannis Antetokounmpo, we know they offered Jaylen Brown for Kevin Durant

text_blocks.speaker: Monica McNutt
text_blocks.text: Everyone couldn't believe their eyes yesterday seeing that Jaylen Brown is now a 76er. How did this trade come to be?

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: The Celtics had made the decision a long time ago. When you dangle Jaylen Brown in trade talks with Giannis Antetokounmpo, we know they offered Jaylen Brown for Kevin Durant in 2022. And now four years later, after winning Finals MVP, after being an MVP finalist this season, they still were willing to move on from him. They missed out on Giannis. And then after that, a strange thing happened. They continued to have trade conversations. They couldn't get a premium player like a Giannis, but they pursued a package of four, five first-round draft picks. That was not attainable on the open market. But what you have though, is when you shop a player of Jaylen Brown's caliber, it comes with fallout. Him understanding and finding out that he's being dangled, the disrespect that comes with that, what he feels, how it rubs him. And so there were hard conversations that took place between the Celtics and Jaylen Brown. There was no formal trade request by Brown, but everyone around the league understood, given how many times he's been put out there, he would have welcomed a trade at the end of it. And so the bar continued to fall as time went on, and went from four to five firsts to what we ended up seeing, which is Mike Gange, the new president of basketball operations in Philadelphia, stuck with it.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to avoid future contract extension issues
quotes.excerpt: They clearly were not ready to give Jaylen Brown a two-year $145 million supermax contract extension come July.
quotes.quote: Mike Gange, the new president of basketball operations in Philadelphia, stuck with it. They didn't exit the party like some teams did, and they were there at the end with Paul George, a couple first-round picks, and a couple seconds, and they got this deal done because they stuck with it. And at the end of the day, the Celtics knew there was a hard conversation coming in July. They clearly were not ready to give Jaylen Brown a two-year $145 million supermax contract extension come July. So this ultimately makes sure that they got rid of this dilemma, this issue, before they had to face it.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins calls the Jaylen Brown trade a historic mistake
quotes.excerpt: It was one of the dumbest trades in NBA history.
quotes.quote: It was one of the dumbest trades in NBA history. And Mike Gange, Jamil Nelson, Bob Myers, they should be serving breakfast in bed to Brad Stevens. I'm talking about cut up fruit, seedless grapes, mint tea, toast with strawberry jam, because they finesse the hell out of him. And if you're going to trade a guy that's a top-10 player, you at least got to get back a guy that's a top-15, top-20 player, and Paul George is not that. Paul George hasn't been consistently good since I was skinny, and that's been a long damn time.

quotes.speaker: Monica McNutt
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers become a major threat in the Eastern Conference
quotes.excerpt: Philly becomes somebody that you really have to keep an eye on.
quotes.quote: Philly becomes somebody that you really have to keep an eye on. I understand folks being excited about the Raptors and adding Kawhi Leonard to that young group, but when I think of the downhill potential of Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, and you throw V.J. Edgecombe in there, and I would also add, one of my second thoughts was, look what Philly was able to do with barely having Joel Embiid. Is this them continuing to move further and further away from needing to have patience for that process to continue to unfold? The two-way nature that will now be available to a Philadelphia 76ers team that already wants to play with speed, that to me is like, oh, you going to have to watch out for whatever Philly got going on. And they might not be done because it didn't cost them that much.
